overview: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe, on the Black Sea. Its capital and largest city is Bucharest. Romanian is a Romance language, related to Italian, French and Spanish. Romania was a communist state until a revolution in 1989, and it joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007.

geography.text: The Carpathian Mountains curve through the middle of Romania, around the high Transylvanian plateau. Outside the mountains are wide plains, especially in the south, where the Danube forms much of the border with Serbia and Bulgaria. Before reaching the Black Sea, the Danube spreads out into the Danube Delta, a huge wetland that is home to many birds.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot summers and cold, snowy winters, with the Carpathian Mountains in the middle.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Romania has more brown bears than any other European country outside Russia, and the Danube Delta is home to pelicans.

history.text: The land of Romania was the Roman province of Dacia, which is where its Latin-based language comes from. The principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia united in 1859 and became independent of the Ottomans in 1878, and Transylvania joined in 1918. Romania was ruled by communists after the Second World War, and the dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu was overthrown in 1989.

events.title: Union
events.text: Wallachia and Moldavia unite under one ruler.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Romania's independence from the Ottoman Empire is recognised.

events.title: Great Union
events.text: Transylvania and other regions join Romania.

events.title: Revolution
events.text: The communist dictatorship of Ceaușescu is overthrown.

government.text: Romania is a semi-presidential republic. The President, elected directly every five years, leads foreign and defence policy, while the Prime Minister leads the government with the support of parliament. Romania joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007.

economy.text: Romania's economy has grown fast since it joined the EU. Car making, including Dacia, is a major industry, along with IT services, farming and energy. The country has its own currency, the leu.

culture.text: Romanian is a Romance language, like Italian and Spanish, with roots in the Latin spoken in the Roman province of Dacia. Transylvania's castles, such as Bran, are linked in legend to Dracula, a character inspired partly by the ruler Vlad the Impaler. The painted monasteries of Bukovina are covered in bright frescoes.

items.title: Painted monasteries
items.text: Outer walls covered in religious paintings from the 1500s.

items.title: The Danube Delta
items.text: One of Europe's largest wetlands, home to pelicans.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Sarmale, cabbage rolls stuffed with meat, and mămăligă, cornmeal porridge.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The painted monasteries of Bukovina and the sculptures of Brâncuși are national treasures.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On 1 March, people give a mărțișor, a small charm on a red-and-white string, to welcome spring.

sport.text: Gymnastics has brought Romania worldwide fame: Nadia Comăneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history in 1976. Football is the most popular sport, and Gheorghe Hagi led Romania to the 1994 World Cup quarter-finals.

items.title: Nadia Comăneci
items.text: Scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, aged 14.

items.title: Rowing
items.text: Romania's women's eight won Olympic gold four times in a row, from 1996 to 2008.

didYouKnow: Romania's Palace of the Parliament is one of the heaviest buildings in the world.
In the Merry Cemetery at Săpânța, graves are painted in bright colours with funny poems about the people buried there.

keyPeople.name: Nadia Comăneci
keyPeople.text: Scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history, in 1976.

keyPeople.name: Simona Halep
keyPeople.text: Won the French Open in 2018 and Wimbledon in 2019.
